title: which identity declarations sit in a dialect no reader speaks
population_source: the graded rows of E458's faceidentity_latest.json that declare a top-level identity; read sites re-derived from e451.walk_py minus this family's own instruments (e461_/e462_/run_e461/run_e462 + this face); join class carried from identityconsumers_latest.json
method_limits: static: a name is read if a source uses it as a dict key in a read context; a name reached through a composed key (d['card' + '_id']) is invisible and counts as unread, which inflates the silent dialect, never the read one

the never-read set is measured over the same corpus E461 walked, minus this family's own instruments; a field read ONLY by a census instrument would be published as never-read here and is named in fields_whose_read_status_disagrees_with_e461

identity field names in the vocabulary are generic payload keys as often as identity keys ('id' has the most read sites of any name); faces whose read names are all ambiguous are published with a flag rather than folded into the read-only class
contradiction compares declared VALUES as strings; two ids that differ only in case/spacing are reported as a contradiction and must be read from the row
